title: Treasuries Rise After Fed’s Waller Notes Inflation Progress
summary: Treasuries rose after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be inclined to leave interest rates unchanged as long as inflation continues to slow.

title: Stocks, Bonds Rise as Fed-Hike Bets Ease on Waller: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks rose and bond yields fell as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing.

title: Yen Rises as Intervention, BOJ Rate Hike Risks Jolt Traders
summary: The yen strengthened 2% Thursday, reversing a month of gradual decline, as traders lifted bets on Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes and remained vigilant to the risk of official action to further boost the currency.

title: Odd Lots: What the Fed Needs to Do to Shrink Its Balance Sheet
summary: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Stanford Professor Darrell Duffie joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal to discuss what's driving the surge in US government bond yields and what the Fed could do to shrink its balance sheet. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Your ETF of the Moment: Riding the Wild, War-Fueled Oil Market
summary: The US-Israel war with Iran and the inability of Donald Trump to extricate himself from it have made one fund a good bet.

title: Blackstone Private Credit Fund Again Caps Redemptions at 5%
summary: Blackstone Inc. moved to limit redemptions from its flagship private credit fund for a second consecutive quarter, providing an early glimpse at the lasting pressures facing the $1.8 trillion market.

title: Gold Jumps as Traders Weigh Yen Intervention Risk, Fedspeak
summary: Gold rose the most in two weeks as the dollar tumbled against the yen and traders reacted to remarks from policymakers on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

title: S&P 500 Rises After Fed’s Waller Signals Patience on Rate Hikes
summary: The S&P 500 Index rose Thursday as investors weighed remarks from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who offered optimism that inflation is showing some signs of slowing. Traders pared bets for interest-rate hikes in September.

title: EU to See Progress on Savings Union by Year-End, Irish PM Says
summary: Progress on the European Union’s long-awaited savings and investment union will be possible by the end of the year, according to Ireland’s prime minister, Taoiseach Micheal Martin.

title: Campbell’s Shares Slump on Sales Drop, Dividend Cut, Outlook
summary: Campbell’s Co. shares slumped after the packaged food and snack maker posted its fourth straight quarterly sales decline, cut its dividend and unveiled a cost-savings plan.

title: Why Nuveen’s Rodriguez Is ‘Fairly Neutral’ on Duration
summary: Tony Rodriguez, head of fixed income strategy at Nuveen, explains his firm’s position on duration and how that would change with a series of interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: A $5 Billion Bond Revamp Starts Clock on Senegal Default
summary: Senegal has been at the front of emerging-market bond investors’ minds since the government discovered billions of dollars of hidden debt two years ago.

title: Blackstone’s BCRED Limits Redemptions Again
summary: Blackstone limited redemptions from its Blackstone Private Credit Fund to 5% after investors sought to pull shares. Swetha Gopinath has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bonds Are 'Dazed and Confused,' Says Emily Roland
summary: Emily Roland, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife Investment Management, says the firm still likes stocks, but it's time to let bonds do more of the work in investor portfolios. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump’s Oil Deal Lifts Venezuela Bonds Ahead of Debt Rework
summary: Venezuelan bonds have jumped since the Trump administration moved to take control of a huge swath of the country’s oil reserves, with investors factoring in the prospect of higher crude production as they await a debt restructuring that could top $200 billion.

title: Cerba Seeks Court-Supervised Restructuring of €5 Billion Debt
summary: Cerba Healthcare has filed a request to start court-supervised restructuring proceedings in France as the private laboratories company attempts to tackle a debt pile of around €5 billion ($5.8 billion), according to a document seen by Bloomberg News.

title: European Stocks Gain as Fed Rate Hike Wagers Ease; Soitec Jumps
summary: European stocks gained as traders reduced bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike following remarks from Governor Christopher Waller, while Deutsche Telekom AG gained on news that activist investor Elliott Investment Management has built a sizeable stake.

title: Waller Says August CPI Is Key to a Rate Decision
summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said his next decision on interest rates will be “heavily influenced” by August inflation data due next week. Waller says if inflation comes in hot, he'd consider a rate hike. Waller said this in remarks prepared for an event hosted by Reuters. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russia’s Oil Revenue Sinks to Six-Month Low as Urals Price Drops
summary: Russia’s oil revenue slumped to a six-month low in August, reflecting lower export prices and compounding pressure on the Kremlin’s ability to finance its war in Ukraine.

title: Saudi Firm Humain Eyes $2.5 Billion Fund to Build Data Centers
summary: Artificial intelligence firm Humain is planning to raise an initial $2.5 billion from global and domestic investors for a fund to invest in data centers in Saudi Arabia, according to people familiar with the matter.
